reason: E1 shows that thermal exposure at 800 °C forms Cr2O3 and enhances wear resistance for a similar FeCoNiMnCu coating, directly supporting the oxide formation and wear benefit premises. However, E2 reports wear data at unspecified temperature (likely room temperature) without oxide characterization, so it does not support the high-temperature oxide-mediated mechanism or the pre-treatment effect. The hypothesis overstates the evidence by implying E2 supports the high-temperature oxide mechanism when it does not.
premises: Thermal exposure of FeNiCrCoCu coating in air at 800 °C forms a protective oxide layer containing Cr2O3
Formation of this oxide layer enhances wear resistance
The oxide layer reduces direct metal contact and further oxidation during wear
A continuous, adherent Cr-rich oxide film is the key structural mediator for wear protection
Pre-forming the oxide layer via thermal pre-treatment will lower wear rate and friction coefficient at high temperature
